chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Aamir ibn Ameyra, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'It has reached me from you that you said: If a man died and had not performed the Hajj of Islam, and some of his family performed Hajj on his behalf, would that suffice for him?' He said, 'Yes. I bear witness to this from my father, that he narrated to me that a man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, my father died and did not perform Hajj.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Perform Hajj on his behalf, for that will suffice for him.'

key_terms.أَشْهَدُ بِهَا: I bear witness to it / I confirm it
key_terms.حَجَّةَ الْإِسْلَامِ: The obligatory Hajj performed once in a lifetime

ai.seo_question: Does performing Hajj on behalf of a deceased parent suffice if they died without performing it?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of vicarious Hajj (Hajj al-Niyabah) for a deceased who died without fulfilling the obligatory pilgrimage, a ruling confirmed by Imam al-Sadiq (as) through a chain tracing back to the Prophet (saww). It highlights the Shia scholarly consensus that the duty of Hajj al-Islam is transferable, allowing heirs to discharge the spiritual debt of the deceased, thereby ensuring the completion of their religious obligations.
